plan.contextChunk: This figure contains six panels (a through f) arranged in a 3×2 grid, each showing the scalar output y of a trained shallow one-hidden-layer neural network as a function of a scalar input x ∈ [0, 1]. The panels correspond to networks with increasing numbers of hidden units — 6, 7, 8, 10, and 50, plus one additional configuration — with each panel’s title indicating the hidden unit count. Each panel has a horizontal axis labeled “Input, x” and a vertical axis labeled “Output, y”; the y-axis range spans approximately [0, 1] or [−1, 1] depending on the panel. With more hidden units the output function is relatively simple and smooth, while as the hidden unit count decreases the function develops more oscillations and finer local structure. This figure illustrates how the capacity of a shallow neural network — and hence the complexity and expressiveness of the functions it can represent — scales with the number of hidden units.

interactionPlan.concept: Increasing the number of hidden units in a shallow neural network changes the capacity of the fitted function, altering how smoothly or intricately it can match the observed training data.
elements: six small-multiple panels arranged in a 3-by-2 grid labeled a), b), c), d), e), f)
panel a) reference plot with black smooth target curve and orange training data points
panel b) titled '6 hidden units'
panel c) titled '7 hidden units'
panel d) titled '8 hidden units'
panel e) titled '10 hidden units'
panel f) titled '50 hidden units'
shared horizontal axis labeled 'Input, x'
shared vertical axis labeled 'Output, y'
x-axis tick labels at 0.0, 0.5, and 1.0 in each panel
y-axis tick labels around -1.0, 0.0, and 1.0 in each panel
black smooth underlying function curve repeated in each panel
orange circular training data points repeated in each panel
pale cyan fitted neural-network curve in panels b) through f)
rectangular black border around each subplot
minor tick marks on axes

interactions.label: Number of hidden units
interactions.teaches: The learner sees that changing the number of hidden units changes the expressive capacity of the shallow network and therefore the shape of the fitted regression curve.
The learner can isolate one hidden-unit configuration and inspect how closely that fitted curve follows the data points versus the smoother underlying trend.

interactions.label: Compare capacity extremes
interactions.teaches: The learner directly contrasts a low-capacity fit with a high-capacity fit and understands that hidden-unit count controls the complexity available to the model.

demo_steps.title: Reference data and target trend
demo_steps.narration: The orange points are the training observations, while the black curve shows the smooth underlying relationship the model is trying to approximate.

demo_steps.title: Low hidden-unit count
demo_steps.narration: With 6 hidden units, the cyan network fit has limited flexibility and uses a small number of broad piecewise segments to pass near the data.

demo_steps.title: Intermediate capacity
demo_steps.narration: As the slider moves through 7, 8, and 10 hidden units, the fitted curve gains more degrees of freedom and can better adapt to local structure in the observations.

demo_steps.title: High hidden-unit count
demo_steps.narration: At 50 hidden units, the network has enough capacity to trace a much smoother and more detailed approximation of the target curve while still matching the training points.

demo_steps.title: Inspect one panel closely
demo_steps.narration: Click any panel to enlarge that hidden-unit setting and compare the cyan fitted curve against both the orange observations and the black reference function.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Hidden units are the capacity knob: changing their number changes how much shape complexity the shallow network can express.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the figure as six aligned line-plot panels with consistent x-range from 0 to 1 and y-range roughly from -1 to 1. Use a thick black smooth curve for the reference function, orange filled circles for the same training samples in every panel, and a thick pale cyan curve for the learned network fit in the hidden-unit panels. The cyan fit should look piecewise and angular for low hidden counts, then increasingly close to the black curve as hidden units rise, especially in the 50-hidden-unit panel. Keep titles large above panels b through f, panel letters in the upper-left corners, and axis labels large on the outer plots.
